answer: In a marketplace for tending a virtual garden, an agent named juniper or umber must lock a separate 100-credit bond before it can bid. If an audit proves an agent submitted a forged work receipt, the market seizes its bond. Running 1,000 fake bidders therefore ties up 100,000 credits at once, and each identity caught cheating costs the attacker 100 credits. New names are free; active bidders are not.
